title: The nonexistence conjecture for polynomial enumeration of divisor-count classes
statement: For $k$ with $0<k<n$, define $A_{2k}=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\nu(n)=2k\}$, where $\nu(n)$ is the number of positive divisors of $n$. **The divisor-class polynomial conjecture.** No polynomial in $n$ generates the elements of $A_{2k}$ successively. The claim is presented as an extension of the asserted nonexistence of a polynomial generating all primes successively, but the source gives no resolution evidence.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04522

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).
source_name: Yeisson Alexis Acevedo Agudelo, “Prime numbers. An alternative study using ova-angular rotations”, arXiv:2104.04522 (2021).
